beat.title: Beat grid and quantization
beat.disabled: No manual grid. Actions use immediate mode.
beat.invalid: BPM: 20–600; beats per bar: 1–32; finite origin within ±1e9 seconds.
beat.manual_help: Timing follows this manual grid. Tap tempo needs four taps; it does not detect the downbeat. Pending actions wait while paused.
beat.source_changed: Cancelled: playback position or work changed.
beat.no_grid: Enable a beat grid before quantizing.
beat.no_boundary: No further beat within the time limit.
beat.target_unavailable: Target unavailable. Current work is retained.
project.beat_schema: Beat metadata does not match the project version.

beat.wait_plan: Wait for the current graph to compile before recalling.
help.route.event: Connect to event inputs: envelopes, steps, gates, latches or optional state reset. Preview bars count events between samples; # is the cumulative count and @ is the last event time.
event.rejected_reports: Event rejection reports since reset (some triggers were skipped)
help.event.beat: Emit on the project beat grid. Enable and configure that grid first. The first evaluation establishes a baseline without replaying past beats.
help.event.cue: Emit when playback crosses a snapshot Cue. Seek does not replay skipped Cues.
help.event.audio_onset: Emit once per newly detected onset above the selected-band threshold. Time is the observing display frame, including FFT detection delay. Requires an active audio input.
help.event.edge: Convert scalar threshold crossings into rising pulses or explicit gate on/off events, with hysteresis to suppress jitter.
help.event.merge: Merge in timestamp order and deduplicate shared event identities. At most 256 events per output batch.
help.event.envelope: Timestamp-based linear ADSR. Pulses release after duration; gate-off releases from the current amplitude. Reset clears the envelope.
help.event.step: Advance a bounded integer step on pulse or gate-on, wrapping in both directions. Reset restores the initial index.
help.event.gate: Pulse toggles the gate; explicit gate events set it. While open, output follows the value input; otherwise output is zero.
help.event.latch: Capture the value input on the triggering frame and hold it. Reset restores the initial value.
help.event.reset: Convert pulse or gate-on to a reset event. Connect only to the state nodes you intend to restart; gate-off is ignored.
event.beat_grid_required: Enable and configure the project beat grid before connecting this beat event.
help.event.input: Replay an action track and accept local live actions. Connect envelopes, steps, gates or resets. Record from a root-graph input; embedded component tracks also replay.
event.track_help: Stable action IDs, media seconds, kind and value; up to 4096 actions per track. Apply edits explicitly.
event.graph_track_limit: The expanded graph exceeds 16384 recorded actions. Split the work or reduce its actions.
event.select_live_input: Select a connected root action input and start playback. Wait for the current graph to be ready; keep the same target during a take.
event.recording_help: Records only pulse, gate and reset actions for this input at actual media dispatch time. Existing actions keep replaying. Pause disables triggering; seeking or editing interrupts the take. Finish creates one undo step. Unrecorded audio, live macros and other inputs are not captured.
event.recording_full: The action track is full; further actions were not recorded. Finish to retain the recorded take.
event.take_interrupted: Time, project or runtime state changed; the uncommitted take was cancelled.
event.take_target_changed: The project or action target was edited; the uncommitted take was cancelled.
event.pending_actions: Actions are waiting for the next graph evaluation.
event.input_rejected: Some actions were rejected. Check event budgets and the current state.
event.take_saved: Take finished. Save the project to retain its action track.
event.take_cancelled: Take discarded; the original track is retained.
event.invalid_action: Invalid action: time must be 0–1 billion seconds and pulse value must be finite within ±1 million.

help.point.spectrum: Sample canonical log-frequency bands into ordered points. Magnitude controls position and color; connect to point rendering, paths or geometry instances. X/Y are normalized by canvas width/height independently: radial points appear elliptical on a wide canvas, while world paths use their projection span. Silence retains the baseline.
help.gpu.texture_sample: Sample the image at each GPU point center to control color, alpha and size. Original points stay unchanged; preview the result or connect it to GPU point rendering. To combine maps, composite the textures before sampling.
graph.gpu_sample_chain: A point view supports one texture sample. Composite multiple textures first, then sample them from the original GPU points.
